text: Let $g:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be a non constant twice differentiable function such that $\mathrm{g}^{'}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=\mathrm{g}^{'}\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )$. If a real valued function $f$ is defined as $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}[g(x)+g(2-x)]$, then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Differentiating, with the chain rule on $g(2-x)$:

$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{1}{2}[g^{'}(x)-g^{'}(2-x)]$

and $f^{'}$ is differentiable because $g$ is twice differentiable.

$f^{'}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )=\dfrac{1}{2}\left [g^{'}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )-g^{'}\left (\dfrac{3}{2}\right )\right ]=0,f^{'}(1)=\dfrac{1}{2}[g^{'}(1)-g^{'}(1)]=0,f^{'}\left (\dfrac{3}{2}\right )=\dfrac{1}{2}\left [g^{'}\left (\dfrac{3}{2}\right )-g^{'}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )\right ]=0$

Rolle's theorem applied to $f^{'}$ on $\left [\dfrac{1}{2},1\right ]$ and on $\left [1,\dfrac{3}{2}\right ]$ gives $f^{''}(c_{1})=0$ for some $c_{1}\in \left (\dfrac{1}{2},1\right )$ and $f^{''}(c_{2})=0$ for some $c_{2}\in \left (1,\dfrac{3}{2}\right )$. So $f^{''}(x)=0$ for at least two $x$ in $(0,2)$.

Option (B) fails because the sum is $0$, (C) fails because $c_{1}\in (0,1)$, and (D) is not guaranteed: for $g(x)=\cos 4πx$, $f^{''}(x)=-16π^{2}\cos 4πx$ vanishes four times in $(0,1)$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: The value of $\lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\frac{n^{3}}{(n^{2}+k^{2})(n^{2}+3k^{2})}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \lim _{n\to \infty }\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{n^{3}}{n^{4}\left (1+\frac{k^{2}}{n^{2}}\right )\left (1+\frac{3k^{2}}{n^{2}}\right )} \\ =\lim _{n\to \infty }\dfrac{1}{n}\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{\left (1+\frac{k^{2}}{n^{2}}\right )\left (1+\frac{3k^{2}}{n^{2}}\right )} \end{array}$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{dx}{3(1+x^{2})\left (\frac{1}{3}+x^{2}\right )}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\int\limits _{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{3}\times \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{\left (x^{2}+1\right )-\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right )}{(1+x^{2})\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right )}dx \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left [\dfrac{1}{x^{2}+\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right ]dx \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\left [\sqrt{3}\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{3}x)\right ]_{0}^{1}-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\tan ^{-1}x\right )_{0}^{1} \\ =\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right )-\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{π}{4}\right )=\dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{3}}-\dfrac{π}{8} \\ =\dfrac{13π}{8\cdot (4\sqrt{3}+3)} \end{array}$

text: Let $\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{a}_{1}\hat{i}+\mathrm{a}_{2}\hat{j}+\mathrm{a}_{3}\hat{k}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{b}_{1}\hat{i}+\mathrm{b}_{2}\hat{j}+\mathrm{b}_{3}\hat{k}$ be two vectors such that $|\vec{\mathrm{a}}|=1,⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=2$ and $|⃗{b}|=4$. If $⃗{c}=2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})-3⃗{b}$, then the angle between $⃗{b}$ and $⃗{c}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $|⃗{a}|=1$, $|⃗{b}|=4$, $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=2$ and $⃗{c}=2(⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})-3⃗{b}$.

Since $⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}$ is perpendicular to $⃗{b}$, $(⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})\cdot ⃗{b}=0$, so

$⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=-3|⃗{b}|^{2}=-48$

The same perpendicularity removes the cross term in $|⃗{c}|^{2}$:

$|⃗{c}|^{2}=4|⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}|^{2}+9|⃗{b}|^{2}$

$|⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}|^{2}=|⃗{a}|^{2}|⃗{b}|^{2}-(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}=16-4=12$, so $|⃗{c}|^{2}=48+144=192$ and $|⃗{c}|=8\sqrt{3}$.

$\cos θ=\frac{⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}}{|⃗{b}||⃗{c}|}=\frac{-48}{4\times 8\sqrt{3}}=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

So $θ=\cos ^{-1}\left (-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

options: The system has unique solution if $λ\neq \frac{1}{2}$ and $μ\neq 1,15$

text: If $z=x+iy,xy\neq 0$, satisfies the equation $z^{2}+i\bar{z}=0$, then $\left |z^{2}\right |$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $z^{2}+i\bar{z}=0$, $z^{2}=-i\bar{z}$. Taking moduli, with $|z^{2}|=|z|^{2}$, $|-i|=1$ and $|\bar{z}|=|z|$:

$|z|^{2}=|z|$

Since $xy\neq 0$, $z\neq 0$, so $|z|=1$.

Such z exist: comparing parts of $x^{2}-y^{2}+2ixy=-y-ix$ gives $2xy=-x\Rightarrow y=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x^{2}-y^{2}=-y\Rightarrow x^{2}=\dfrac{3}{4}$, so $z=\pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{i}{2}$, with $|z|=1$.

Therefore

$\left |z^{2}\right |=|z|^{2}=1$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: The value of $9\int\limits _{0}^{9}\left [\sqrt{\frac{10x}{x+1}}\right ]\mathrm{d}x$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g(x)=\dfrac{10x}{x+1}=10-\dfrac{10}{x+1}$ increases from $0$ at $x=0$ to $9$ at $x=9$, so $\sqrt{g(x)}$ runs from $0$ to $3$ and $\left [\sqrt{g(x)}\right ]$ changes value where $\sqrt{g(x)}=1,2,3$, i.e. where $g(x)=1,4,9$.

$\dfrac{10x}{x+1}=1\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{9},\dfrac{10x}{x+1}=4\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{2}{3},\dfrac{10x}{x+1}=9\Rightarrow x=9$

So $\left [\sqrt{g(x)}\right ]$ is $0$ on $\left [0,\frac{1}{9}\right )$, $1$ on $\left [\frac{1}{9},\frac{2}{3}\right )$, $2$ on $\left [\frac{2}{3},9\right )$, and equals $3$ only at $x=9$.

$9\int\limits _{0}^{9}\left [\sqrt{\dfrac{10x}{x+1}}\right ]dx=9\left [1\left (\dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right )+2\left (9-\dfrac{2}{3}\right )\right ]=9\left (\dfrac{5}{9}+\dfrac{50}{3}\right )=5+150=155$

Hence, the answer is 155.

text: Let $α,β\in 𝐍$ be roots of the equation $x^{2}-70x+λ=0$, where $\frac{λ}{2},\frac{λ}{3}\notin 𝐍$. If $λ$ assumes the minimum possible value, then $\frac{(\sqrt{α-1}+\sqrt{β-1})(λ+35)}{|α-β|}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}-70x+λ=0 \\ α+β=70 \\ αβ=λ \\ \therefore α(70-α)=λ \end{array}$

Since, 2 and 3 do not divide $λ$

$\therefore α=5,β=65,λ=325$

By putting value of $α,β,λ$ we get the required value $60$.

text: Number of integral terms in the expansion of $\left \{7^{\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )}+11^{\left (\frac{1}{6}\right )}\right \}^{824}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term in expansion of $\left ((7)^{1/2}+(11)^{1/6}\right )^{824}$ is $\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}+1}={}^{824}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}(7)^{\frac{824-\mathrm{r}}{2}}(11)^{\mathrm{r}/6}$

For integral term, $r$ must be multiple of 6.

Hence $r=0,6,12,.......822$

text: If $\mathrm{d}_{1}$ is the shortest distance between the lines $x+1=2y=-12z,x=y+2=6z-6$ and $\mathrm{d}_{2}$ is the shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+8}{-7}=\frac{z-4}{5},\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{1}=\frac{z-6}{-3}$, then the value of $\frac{32\sqrt{3}\mathrm{d}_{1}}{\mathrm{d}_{2}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{L}_{1}:\frac{\mathrm{x}+1}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}}{1/2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}}{-1/12},\mathrm{L}_{2}:\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{y}+2}{1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{\frac{1}{6}}$

$\mathrm{d}_{1}=$ shortest distance between $\mathrm{L}_{1}&\mathrm{L}_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\left |\dfrac{\left (⃗{a}_{2}-⃗{a}_{1}\right )\cdot \left (⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}\right )}{\right |\left (⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}\right )\left |}\right | \\ d_{1}=2 \\ \mathrm{L}_{3}:\dfrac{\mathrm{x}-1}{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{y}+8}{-7}=\dfrac{\mathrm{z}-4}{5},\mathrm{L}_{4}:\dfrac{\mathrm{x}-1}{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{y}-2}{1}=\dfrac{\mathrm{z}-6}{-3} \\ \mathrm{d}_{2}=\text{shortest distance between}\mathrm{L}_{3}&\mathrm{L}_{4} \\ \mathrm{d}_{2}=\dfrac{12}{\sqrt{3}}\text{Hence} \\ =\dfrac{32\sqrt{3}\mathrm{d}_{1}}{\mathrm{d}_{2}}=\dfrac{32\sqrt{3}\times 2}{\frac{12}{\sqrt{3}}}=16 \end{array}$

text:
If the function

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{|x|}, & |x|⩾2 \\ \mathrm{a}x^{2}+2\mathrm{b}, & |x|<2 \end{array} \right.$

is differentiable on $𝐑$, then $48(a+b)$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})\left \{\begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}};\mathrm{x}\geq 2 \\ \mathrm{ax}^{2}+2\mathrm{b};-2<\mathrm{x}<2 \\ -\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}};\mathrm{x}\leq -2 \end{array} \right.$

Continuous at $\mathrm{x}=2\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=4\mathrm{a}+2\mathrm{b}$

Continuous at $\mathrm{x}=-2\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=4\mathrm{a}+2\mathrm{b}$

Since, it is differentiable at $\mathrm{x}=2$

$-\frac{1}{x^{2}}=2\mathrm{ax}$

Differentiable at $x=2\Rightarrow \frac{-1}{4}=4a\Rightarrow a=\frac{-1}{16},b=\frac{3}{8}$
